The '''1930 German football championship''', the 23rd edition of the competition, was won by [[Hertha BSC]], defeating [[Holstein Kiel]] 5–4 in the final.<ref name="Rsssf" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duithistpre45.html |title=German championship 1930  |website= Rsssf.com |access-date= 6 January 2016}}</ref>

For Hertha it was the fifth consecutive final the club played in and the first championship the club won, having lost all four previous finals. Hertha would go on to win the 1931 final as well and thereby become only the second club, after [[1. FC Nürnberg]], to defend its title. For Holstein Kiel it was the third and last appearance in the final, having lost the 1910 one and won two years later in 1912, both against [[Karlsruher FV]].<ref name="List" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duitchamp.html |title=(West) Germany -List of champions |website= Rsssf.com |access-date= 6 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/hertha-bsc/1/ |title= Hertha BSC » Steckbrief |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 6 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=Hertha BSC honours}}</ref>

The final itself equaled the then-record of goals scored, nine, set in 1903. Hertha fell behind twice in the game, 0–2 and 2–3, before [[Hans Ruch]] scored the winning ninth goal of the game in the 87th minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/spielbericht/deutsche-meisterschaft-1930-finale-hertha-bsc-holstein-kiel/ |title= Deutsche Meisterschaft 1929/1930 » Finale » Hertha BSC - Holstein Kiel 5:4 |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 6 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=German championship 1929–30: Final}}</ref>

[[1. FC Nürnberg]]'s [[Josef Schmitt (footballer)|Josef Schmitt]] was the top scorer of the 1930 championship with seven goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/deutsche-meisterschaft/ |title=Deutsche Meisterschaft » Torschützenkönige |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 6 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=German championship: Top goal scorer}}</ref>

Sixteen clubs qualified for the knock-out competition, two from each of the regional federations plus an additional third club from the South and West. In all cases the regional champions qualified and almost all of the runners-up, except in Central Germany where the second spot went to the regional cup winner. In the West the third spot went to the third placed team of the championship while, in the South, the third spot was determined in a separate qualifying competition for runners-up and third placed teams.<ref name="Rsssf" />
